timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Welcome to the Water Cube.
You can tell me who you are and where you are from and tell me why you are at World Water Week.
I am the member of parliament. I come from the Kingdom of Sazlens. I have come for water climate change and food security in this part of the world.
In your name sir? My name is Joseph Sosa.
Thank you.
So you are from Sazlens?
Yes please. Tell us what is happening in your country.
Well we have got some challenges there especially with drought.
I see a lot of people here that talk about overflading mostly but my country got a problem with drought.
As a result my people are starving because there is no more rain.
And my government is trying to put up some small items for water so that people can start going some small vegetables.
But unfortunately what I have realized is that the international countries, the only concentrate on countries where there were some wars.
In countries like the Kingdom of Sazlens we have some problems with wars that don't try to have the Kingdom.
They think we are far better yet we have got challenges about drought and also HIV and AIDS.
I would like to urge the international community to also look at Sazlens as a country because we are having some problems as well.
And so with the drought what sorts of solutions are you looking for?
Well if my government can be assisted as far as finds to do some festival to do a feasibility study to see if we cannot construct more dams away we can store or we can harvest water.
So that at the end of the day we can start using the water to grow some crops so that you can feed ourself.
We know this was a very hard-working people very honest and quite reliable but we were just making funds to sustain ourself as far as food is concerned.
And are there, when you say build dams you have some rivers that run through the country?
Definitely we do have rivers and we are sharing with our neighbors like South Africa and Mozambique.
And most of the time our rivers flow to our next country which sometimes have some flooding there.
If we can have some fund we can construct some small dams you know and I hope we have got some international standard of to share water which we still keep that.
We cannot run away from that but otherwise we need fund so that we can expand our project as far as dams are concerned.
Are the countries working together right now?

Yeah the countries are working together and every time you know when we start putting a new dam we always consult each other we don't just go with it because we have got to do it according to the international agreement.
Great thank you for speaking with us.
Thanks very much.

youtube_description: Member of Parliament Joseph Souza talks about the challenges in Swaziland because of drought, resulting food shortages, and what it will take to fix the problems. Interviewed by Beth Whiteside at Stockholm World Water Week, 20 August 2009. (Aug 20, 2009)
